svg.title: How an agent acts without losing control
svg.desc: Drafting, approving, executing and verifying are separate steps with separate evidence.
svg.text: FTA / AGENTIC AI / GITEX / LEARNING GUIDE
How an agent acts without losing control
Drafting, approving, executing and verifying are separate steps with separate evidence.
PROPOSED · 23 NOV 2026
1 Build an action preview
Action Agent prepares a draft or tool request
Exact company, case and affected record IDs
Proposed values and document attachments
2 Human reviews and approves
Show before / after values and the full draft
Allow edit, cancel or approve
Bind approval to the exact payload version
3 Backend rechecks and executes
Recheck role, scope and record freshness
Reject changed or unapproved payloads
Use an idempotency key to prevent repeats
4 Store the real operation status
Return operation ID and committed status
If the outcome is unknown, check status first
Do not blindly repeat a timed-out submission
5 Reconcile the new evidence
Read the submitted disclosure or documents
Run the same validation against the new state
Report unresolved differences explicitly
6 Continue the shared case
Both roles read the same case and events
Record approvals, submissions and checks
Close only when closure conditions are met
PERSISTENT STATE / BACKEND CONTRACT
What must survive a restart, role switch or repeated button press
case_id + company_id + authorized role scope
current workflow stage + completed task IDs
approved payload version + action operation ID
evidence references + instruction versions
event timestamps + separate simulated business dates
Demo clock: move to the next prepared event.
Approval: still required before each effect.
Pending: a valid status, not an automatic closure.
Reset: isolate or clear the visitor session safely.
All external actions stay inside the demo sandbox.
Case/state storage and business APIs are application components to build or integrate; confirm Cloudera runtime support separately.
WORKED EXAMPLE / READ FROM TOP TO BOTTOM
From “please fix it” to a verified demo correction
After reading the explanation, the Al Yasmeen user says: “Prepare the correction.”
STEP / WHO ACTS
WHAT THEY ACTUALLY DO
WHAT COMES BACK / WHY IT MATTERS
Action workflow
Prepares the demo disclosure using the supported changes: Dubai
Preview v1: company, case, affected boxes,
amounts and evidence references.
Human user
Reviews the exact preview and selects Approve. If the user edits
it, the edited version needs fresh approval.
An approval record tied to preview v1. Cancel
produces no submission.
Backend execution
Checks role, company scope, current record version and approval.
Sends the approved request to the demo submission API.
One operation ID. A changed record blocks
execution until the preview is refreshed.
Status tool
If the request times out, checks that operation’s status before
trying again. Reuses its unique operation key.
The same correction is not submitted twice after
a retry or double click.
Reconciliation tool
Reads the resulting return and checks both Emirate boxes and the
invoice evidence against the expected state.
Verified correction, or a specific remaining
difference with a pending/failed status.
Case engine + UI
Records the outcome and shows the same event history in Business
and Inspector views. Advances simulated follow-up events when
needed.
Both roles agree on the case status. “Closed”
requires the closure checks to pass.
What to remember
The agent may prepare a change; the backend controls whether the exact approved change may execute and whether it actually succeeded.
Worked examples use the supplied synthetic draft. Tool behavior and interfaces are proposed; these are not live taxpayer operations.
